newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil govt will reimburse Petrobras subsidies.
newsitem.headline: Brazil govt will reimburse Petrobras subsidies.

text.p: The Brazilian government will reimburse state oil monopoly Petrobras around seven billion reais ($6.73 billion) in subsidies paid over the last 20 years as part of the opening of the oil sector, a congressional deputy said.

Deputy Eliseu Resende, who drew up the bill regulating the opening of the oil and gas sectors, said the government would settle its accounts with Petrobras within a three-year transition period following the approval of the oil bill.
He said the government would study the possibility of raising the necessary funds through the emission of national treasury securities.
Under the oil bill, subsidies for fuel and oil derivatives will be phased out during the three-year transition period.
Resende said fuel and oil derivative prices would probably go up with the elimination of subsidies.
He said the oil bill, which still has to be approved by both houses of Congress, could be in place by the middle of this year.
((--Simona de Logu, Rio de Janeiro newsroom, 5521 507 4151))
